Legacy capacitor banks often operate with simple local controls and may not co- ordinate effectively with other voltage control devices or adapt to changing grid conditions from distributed generation. • Filtersare used to manage harmonic distortion, which occurs when non-linear electrical loads create addi- tional frequencies beyond the standard 60 Hz power frequency, distorting the electrical waveform. Harmonics can cause equipment overheating, interference, and reduced system efficiency. Legacy filters were designed for traditional loads like motors and resistive heating that created predictable harmonic patterns. Modern power electronic devices, including solar inverters, Light-Emitting Diode (LED) lighting, variable frequency drives, and EV chargers, generate different and more complex harmonic profiles that legacy filters may not adequately address. • Variable Frequency Drives (VFD)are power electronic devices that control motor speed by varying fre- quency and voltage, allowing motors to adjust power consumption based on demand. Large Industrial Loads without VFD represent significant inflexible demand that cannot respond to grid conditions or participate in demand response programs. • EV Charging Stationsrepresent a rapidly growing category of grid-connected load equipment. Legacy charging infrastructure consists of simple, unmanaged charging points that draw power at fixed rates without 9 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications coordination with grid conditions. Smart charging stations can communicate with grid operators, adjust charg- ing rates based on grid conditions, and even support Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) applications where vehicles can discharge power back to the grid. With electric vehicles, solar inverters, and other distributed resources creating unprecedented complexity in power flows and grid interactions, modernizing load management equipment transitions from a convenience to a necessity for maintaining grid stability and power quality. 2.2.5 Monitoring and Forecasting Systems Legacy monitoring and forecasting systems often lack the sophisticated capabilities needed for modern grid opera- tions with high renewable generation and dynamic conditions. • Legacy Metersrequire manual reading and provide limited information about electricity usage patterns. Smart meters can be read remotely and may integrate with building control systems, but the transition from legacy meters is still ongoing in many areas. • Weather Sensors and Air Monitoring Sensorssupport grid operations by providing environmental data that affect both generation (particularly renewable resources) and load patterns. Legacy sensors may lack the communication capabilities or data quality needed for advanced forecasting applications. • Forecasting Systemsfor load, solar, and wind prediction are critical for modern grid operations but legacy systems often lack the sophisticated algorithms, data integration capabilities, and real-time updating needed for reliable operation with high renewable generation. • Old Servers and Workstationssupporting grid operations may lack the processing power, security features, and reliability
